Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Pakistan's first innings! The players are already out in the middle. Abdullah Shafique and Imam-ul-Haq are the two openers for Pakistan. Mitchell Starc has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Pakistan, on the other hand, were pretty inconsistent with their line and lengths and allowed the Aussie batters to score runs freely and also gave away a few too many extras. They struggled in the first session of Day 1, but after Lunch, Shaheen Afridi got them the breakthrough while Khurram Shahzad and Aamer Jamal made sure that they sent half of the Australian side back to the hut at Stumps. Agha Salman was very economical with his off-breaks but was unlucky not to pick up a wicket as they dropped a catch and missed a stumping as well on his bowling. They could have restricted the hosts a lot early if their catching was more effective. The pacers struggled again at the start of Day 2, but one bowler stood out for them, and it was Aamer Jamal who registered a brilliant five-wicket haul and ended up with six wickets on debut. Now, it is up to their batters to get close to or past the Aussie total to stay in the Test. Join us in a bit for Pakistan's reply.

Australia have posted a massive first innings total! All eyes were on David Warner with all the outside noise, and he responded in his own style with a smashing hundred scoring 164 runs. They were able to build up a few good partnerships which helped them to keep the runs flowing, and most of their batters got off to good starts as well but couldn't convert them into big scores. However, the local boy, Mitchell Marsh looked determined right from the start and made sure to make his knock a memorable one. He played brilliantly for his 90, but unfortunately, he just missed out on his hundred. The lower order could mot impact much and they will be a bit disappointed of not getting to that 500-run mark, but this is still a big total on this wicket.

Steams in from over the wicket and hurls it on the sixth stump line, on a back of a length, Nathan Lyon is made to play at it due to the angle. The ball holds its line and Lyon gets an outside edge that goes straight into the bread basket of Agha Salman at first slip who does the rest. Australia have been bowled out for 487 in their first innings!

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Can you believe it? Khurram Shahzad strikes with the first delivery after Lunch! Mitchell Marsh falls 10 runs short of what would have been a memorable hundred in front of his home crowd! Khurram Shahzad charges in from over the wicket and bowls it on a good length, angling back in, on off, Mitchell Marsh gives the charge as he looks to launch it down the ground. He pays the price for leaving a big gap between bat and pad as the ball jags back in to beat him on the inside edge and rattles into the middle stump. Khurram Shahzad is thrilled to bits and this is just the start Pakistan were after.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session! The players are making their way out to the middle now. Mitchell Marsh and Pat Cummins to continue the batting for Australia. Khurram Shahzad to bowl the first over after Lunch.
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

As far as Pakistan are concerned, it was another tough session for them where they toiled hard without much success. The debutant Aamer Jamal has been one of the few bright spots for them and is now a wicket away from his maiden Test five-wicket haul. Having started the day on the back foot, Pakistan needed a good first session to fight their way back into the game. Despite having the second new ball, which was around 3 overs old, Shaheen Afridi and Khurram Shahzad were pretty inconsistent, which meant that there was no pressure created on the Aussie batters. Just when it looked like the wheels were starting to come off for Pakistan, Aamer Jamal produced a peach to get rid of Alex Carey before accounting for Mitchell Starc a few overs later. However, the rest of the bowling unit was not able to offer support from the other end and now Pakistan have their backs against the wall. Will we see some fight from Pakistan? Join us back at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) for the post-Lunch session to find out.

SESSION SUMMARY - 130 runs, 26 overs, and 2 wickets. As it did on Day 1, the first session has yet again belonged to Australia! They have added 130 runs to their overnight score of 346 and now find themselves in a commanding position. It was a watchful start to Day 2 from Alex Carey and Mitchell Marsh for Australia. Marsh was the first to get off the blocks, while Carey also got into the act as he grew in confidence. Marsh, the aggressor of the two batters, notched up his fifth Test fifty, and his 90-run stand with Carey took Australia to an even stronger position. Despite the fall of a couple of wickets, Marsh carried on and thanks to the support from Pat Cummins, he is now 10 runs away from a century on his home ground. Australia will be pretty pleased with this total they have got so far but they would want to bat Pakistan out of the game and will be on the hunt for an even bigger score.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin Day 2! The Pakistan players can be seen in a huddle who then spread out to take their respective field positions. Alex Carey and Mitchell Marsh are ready to continue the innings for Australia. Shaheen Afridi to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...

On the other hand, it was not a great day for Pakistan, as the bowlers were having difficulties finding the perfect line and length to create problems for the Aussie batters. Shaheen Afridi needs to buckle up as the senior bowler to take a few more wickets and clear up the lower middle order and the tail-enders on Day 2, as the visitors have already conceded too many runs for the first innings. They have to re-strategize the whole plan as the match is slipping away from their hands. They were also a bit sloppy in the fielding, so they have to step up in that department too. Will Pakistan fight back on Day 2? We shall find out soon, as the first ball is not far away.

The defending World Test Champions are all set after a terrific performance on Day 1. The top batters have done their part, especially the pocket dynamo, David Warner, who scored 164 runs in 211 deliveries, taking advantage of home conditions. The situation is totally under the control of the Aussies, as at the post-match interview on Day 1, the skipper, Pat Cummins, stated that they would need 100 or 150 more runs on Day 2 for his bowlers to bowl with. It will be all in the hands of Mitchell Marsh, Alex Carey, and the skipper, Pat Cummins, to stretch the score as much as they can.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of Day 2 of the first Test between Australia and Pakistan at the Perth Stadium for the Benaud-Qadir Trophy. The excitement is palpable as the match between these two sides turns into a curveball.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from this eventful Day 1 of the 'West Test' where Australia find themselves in a strong position while Pakistan did pull things back a bit but still needs to do a lot of work. Day 2 will start on 15th December, Friday at 7.50 am IST (2.20 am GMT), but as you know, you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Pat Cummins, the skipper of Australia is up for a chat! He expresses it was close to a perfect day. Continues that they weren't sure about what to do at the toss, but says they are content with how things unfolded. He praises David Warner and says that he is a legendary player and he's being aggressive, putting the pressure back on Pakistan. Adds that he's making it look easier than it is and it was a brilliant inning from him. Concludes by saying that another 100-150 runs would be great.

In the second session, Pakistan started well with both pacers troubling the batters. Shaheen Afridi drew first blood by getting rid of Usman Khawaja while Faheem Ashraf dismissed Marnus Labuschagne cheaply as well. However, they allowed the hosts to build up a couple of partnerships before and after Tea. Warner smashed his 26th Test century to silence the critics while Steven Smith and Travis Head also contributed well but both will be disappointed about not converting their starts. Khurram Shahzad struggled with No Balls in both sessions but got Smith as his first Test wicket while Aamer Jamal removed Head. Warner was dropped on 104 and also survived a stumping chance, and went on to punish the visitors even more as he scored 164 runs before falling victim to short ball tactics eventually giving away his wicket to Aamer Jamal. Mitchell Marsh and Alex Carey stood strong out in the middle till the end negotiating a few overs from the second new ball as well, and they will look to add more runs to make this already big total, even bigger.

The two Aussie openers proved Pat Cummins' decision to bat first correct as they went aggressively right from the start. They did survive a few scares and Usman Khawaja was also dropped by Abdullah Shafique early on which proved to be a bit costly for the visitors. David Warner and Khawaja added over 100 runs before Lunch with the former registering a quick-fire fifty as well which put the hosts in a commanding position. The Pakistani pacers struggled with their line and lengths and their lead bowler, Shaheen Afridi went for a few too many runs. They were able to find some rhythm just before the end of the first session with Agha Salman also using his off-breaks well to check the runs but without any rewards.

A fantastic Day 1 for the Aussies comes to an end! The highlight was of course the smashing big daddy hundred from the 'Pocket Dynamo', David Warner. He also went past Matthew Hayden and Michael Clarke to break into the top 5 leading run-scorers for Australia in Test cricket. That exceptional knock helped the Aussies to end the Day with 346 runs with still half their side left to bat. Pakistan were outplayed in the first session but in the next two sessions, they were able to pull things back a bit especially after Tea. The visitors will look to make early inroads on Day 2 to get through to the lower order of the hosts and wrap things up as quickly as possible.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the third and final session of Day 1. Pakistan players are seen in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse to take their respective field positions. David Warner and Steven Smith are all set to resume their innings for Australia. Khurram Shahzad is at the top of his mark and is raring to go. Let's play...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

The man of the moment, David Warner is in for a chat. He says that it was his job to come out and score runs. Shares that his plan was to put pressure on the Pakistan bowlers. Mentions that it is just another Test match hundred for Australia. Feels that the wicket is nice and there are a lot of runs to be had here. On his celebration, he says that there cannot be a better way to silence the critics.

An entertaining session comes to an end! Session Summary - 93 runs and 2 wickets in 25 overs. After a dominant first session from Australia, it was Pakistan who started on the front foot after Lunch. Khurram Shahzad and Shaheen Afridi hit the right lengths beating both batters left, right, and centre. The latter finally managed to force a nick and got rid of Usman Khawaja, but that did not slow down David Warner as he held one end brilliantly. Marnus Labuschagne could not stick around for long as he was dismissed LBW by Shahzad who otherwise struggled with No Balls in this session as well. Warner brought up his stunning hundred silencing the haters in his own fashion. He was also dropped on 104 by Khurram Shahzad as he and Steven Smith ended the session strongly adding over 50 runs together. Pakistan pulled things back earlier in the session but they will be hoping to do a lot more in the last session or else this game could get away from them pretty quickly. Join us at 12.50 pm IST (7.20 am GMT) to see how the third session pans out.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the second session to commence. The two umpires make their way out to the middle. Shan Masood leads his troops out to the centre and they are joined by the two Australian openers, David Warner and Usman Khawaja. It will be Shaheen Afridi to start the proceedings with the ball in the post-Lunch session. Off we go...
... DAY 1, SESSION 2 ...

As the scoreboard suggests, it was a tough session for Pakistan. Having lost the toss, Pakistan needed early breakthroughs, and given that there are two debutants in the side, their hopes rested on Shaheen Afridi. The left-arm seamer was all over the place with his lines and lengths, which did not help Khurram Shahzad's cause who was disciplined from the other end. Although Afridi did find his groove later in his spell, the two openers were well set by then. Brought on as the first change, Aamer Jamal started decently and it was unfortunate that Abdullah Shafique failed to hang on the catch of Usman Khawaja when he was on 21 off his bowling. Faheem Ashraf was expensive while Agha Salman has been tidy in the 3 overs bowled so far. All is not lost though for Pakistan as the surface is offering help when bowled in the right areas. Can the visitors manage to make early inroads in the second session? Join us back at 10.30 am IST (5 am GMT) to see how it all pans out.

Australia have absolutely bossed the first session on the opening day of the first Test! If the proceedings of the first session are anything to go by, Pakistan are in for a long day at the office. After Pat Cummins won the toss and opted to put runs on the board, it was a strong start from David Warner and Usman Khawaja. Both openers mixed caution with aggression as they were decisive in leaving good deliveries but made sure to punish freebies offered to them. Playing in what might well be his final Test series, Warner raced to fifty off 41 balls while Khawaja was happy to take the back seat in this partnership which currently stands unbeaten on 117. With the surface expected to get better to bat as the day progresses, David Warner and Usman Khawaja will look to pile on the misery in the post-Lunch session.
